gaps.sentence: If people ___ less time on their phones, they would read more.
gaps.explanation: An unreal present habit takes the past simple in the if-clause: spent.

gaps.sentence: If I ___ the answer, I would tell you immediately.
gaps.explanation: The speaker does not know now, so the if-clause takes the past simple: knew.

gaps.sentence: They would have won the match if their best player ___ injured.
gaps.hint: unreal past needs the past perfect
gaps.explanation: The unreal past condition requires the past perfect: had not been.

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ to your advice — then I would not be in this mess.
gaps.hint: regret about the past, past perfect
gaps.explanation: 'Wish' plus the past perfect expresses regret about the past: had listened.

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ so much cake — I feel sick now.
gaps.hint: past act with a present consequence
gaps.explanation: The regret is about a past action, so 'wish' takes the past perfect: had not eaten.

gaps.sentence: If it ___ tomorrow, the match will be cancelled.
gaps.explanation: In first conditionals the if-clause takes the present simple even with future meaning: rains.

gaps.sentence: Unless the strike ___, flights will be grounded all weekend.
gaps.hint: unless plus a present passive verb
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' clauses use the present simple, here in the passive: is called off.

gaps.sentence: If the red light ___, the machine needs servicing.
gaps.hint: a general rule stated with if
gaps.explanation: Rules and general facts use the present simple in the if-clause: flashes.
